publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Independently reviewed by a second agent; not human scholarly approval.

handDesc.handNote: Brown main writing and darker interventions are visible. Ink differences are recorded without assigning historical hands.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century; this does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Library digital facsimile, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest identifies the images as Public Domain Mark 1.0. Every verse in folios 61v, 62r, 62v, 63r was inspected for this first pass.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first pass of all 106 manuscript verses. No other witness or normalized edition was used as transcription input. Existing annotation coordinates provide navigation, not text. There are 212 annotation rows for 106 distinct source lines. Each pair differs in rectangle bounds but not page. Select the last existing row per verse, except 32 and 43 where the first row includes the baseline otherwise clipped by the last. Every selected rectangle was inspected against the full page; no coordinates were invented and annotations.json is unchanged. sourceWitness=LL and panelId identify annotation provenance only; no LL text was consulted.

correction.p: Uncertain letters are marked unclear and unreadable text gap. Darker ink is hi, not proof of erasure or a distinct hand. Actual additions use add; deletion or substitution is asserted only with visible evidence and qualified where needed. No unattested earlier reading is supplied.

normalization.p: Single source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs and long s are represented with standard Latin characters. Source spelling is preserved; word spacing and couplet layout are editorial. Explicit abbreviation expansions remain in TEI choices. Punctuation and unusual signs are schematic typographic equivalents, not exact pen-shape replicas.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and separation or insertion marks are retained. No modern sentence punctuation is supplied.

segmentation.p: Each l is one verse and one physical source line. The inset of the second line in each couplet follows the visible source layout on folios 61v–63r. The amount is a readable approximation of the manuscript offset; lg groups are editorial elegiac couplets. Each verse has a stable ID and an existing facsimile rectangle. The rectangles may include neighbouring text and need not enclose marginal inscriptions.

interpretation.p: All 106 extant verses and all editorial notes received an independent second image reading. Supported corrections are applied; irrecoverable uncertainty remains localized and documented. No consequential unresolved decision requires user escalation.

revisionDesc.change: First source pass covering all 106 verses and visible interventions in folios 61v, 62r, 62v, 63r; awaiting a different agent's independent reading.

Independently inspected all 106 source verses and every note against full pages and enlarged images. Corrected source readings and punctuation, preserved additions/cancellations/marks and local uncertainty, and confirmed alternating insets from full-page layout.

div.head: Source observations and independently reviewed uncertainties
div.note: Enlarged A opens the poem. A dark t is visible in obsite. Following it, two brown shapes read tentatively pe and are crossed by a horizontal stroke; cancellation is visible, but the cancelled reading remains uncertain. No erased earlier state is inferred.
The written neque and darker supralinear c are both confirmed; no deletion of que is visible.
The image reads turpi grassas; these spellings are retained without grammatical normalization.
Enlargement resolves the final words as dedisse quieti, correcting dedissequenti. The dark/disturbed o-region in properasse remains qualified; no earlier letter is supplied.
The initial is an isolated S before tamen; no separate i is visible. The encoding does not silently supply one.
A darker e is visible within cerealia, without evidence for a recoverable earlier letter.
The final word is written amas with a nasal bar over a; amans is the explicit expansion.
The written sequence is quid esse amor. No final t is supplied after esse.
Main-line meliae has media written above it. Both are retained as a source alternative; the brown word is not declared erased. Main-line bithynide is preserved.
Darker strokes occupy the beginning rap of rapuit. The present reading is legible; no previous reading or hand is assigned.
The main name reads alphion and a small e is added above the i-region. Both layers are retained without flattening to a normalized name.
The darker e regions in Te and penee are retained. A small ring-like supralinear mark is also visible above penee and is recorded without assigning a function or correction history.

The compact initial name is tentatively Pthietum, with ad above its middle. It is not normalized to a familiar geographical name. The first duplicate rectangle contains the full baseline; the second clips its lower part.
A small oblique stroke stands above querere. It is retained as an unspecified source mark, without adding a verbal reading.
The source has a before the et ligature in a-et-olia. The omitted a is restored, with the et ligature still encoded in situ; no normalization to plain etolia.
A left-margin angle-like mark accompanies the initial of Ille; the source per hostia wording is confirmed. The mark is not treated as verse text.

The main-line names ebanthe and esopiae are confirmed. Supralinear eu is legible; beneath final ae of esopiae are two cancellation dots, with darker de above. The ae/de substitution is now encoded. The right margin has eosopide and a fainter tentative asopide, whose faded reading remains qualified. A darker u in Fertur is retained; no historical hand is inferred.
The source reads amplecti, correcting amplexus. Dark initial s of salmonida and final t of posset are confirmed. The first existing duplicate rectangle includes the full baseline.
The final a of iussa is dark; the source colon after aquam is retained.
The horizontal stroke after pomifera is retained as an unspecified mark. The following rua remains tentative. A visible terminal point is restored.
The disturbed/darker erat remains tentative without an invented erased state. A visible oblique supralinear stroke at Ilia is also retained as a mark.
The c of delictaque has darker strokes. A colon-like end mark is retained.
The visible main verb reads Errabant, including n before t. It is not silently normalized.
Independent enlargement supports teris, with one r and darker final s, followed by legible anxia. These source readings replace terris and remove unnecessary uncertainty on anxia.
A dark t is visible in laomedonte; no earlier state is claimed.
The final a of sola is darker and is retained as the current letter.
The written opening is Vitta nec followed by the et ligature and uinctis. The seemingly redundant sequence is preserved.
The adjective before plangis is tentatively insana; mottling and small initial strokes prevent confidence. No reading is borrowed from another witness.
The d of durum is markedly dark; only this present feature is encoded.
The source reads Qui tenero lacrimis, correcting teneris. In ore and the darker e of uidet are confirmed.
The e of pone is dark. The compact nra abbreviation is explicitly expanded as nostra.
The source amnes is confirmed, with a colon-like stop after it and a terminal point after metus restored.
The whole source verse is confirmed; its visible terminal point is now retained.
A dark c stands above the initial Ne. The written Ne and addition are retained together without inventing a deletion.
A small e is written above the final a-region of feras. The main-line a remains visible; both layers are encoded.
Darker letters occur in illa, initial h of humum, and final a of deiecta. The nasal bar on i is explicitly expanded as in.
Darker tepido is written above the still-legible teneros, preceded by a small mark. The mark is retained schematically without assigning a definite function; no main-line deletion is asserted.

A small brown group after molita is crossed by two horizontal strokes. Its tentative m is enclosed in unclear within del. The visible cancellation is retained without inventing securely legible cancelled text.
Enlarged source reading supports Currenti uires eripuere metu. The compact spacing is separated editorially.
Scindes carries a nasal bar over e and is explicitly expanded scindens.
The t of tremente has darker strokes; no preceding reading is supplied.
The o of patrioque is darker. The opening O utinam is separated editorially.

The crossed group after Condita remains tentatively m. The verb appears poterunt, with its post-r vowel still qualified, rather than supplied potuerunt. Supralinear tegi has a preceding small sign, now also encoded; main legi remains visible and is not declared cancelled.

The source sequence is tentatively inuitor a followed by a darker d and ullis. This corrects the first-pass inuitata reading, but the disturbed inuitor region remains unclear. No erased earlier wording or historical hand is invented.
The source reads inficianda, correcting infitianda. Its question-like terminal mark is retained schematically.
The source has uolgi with a visible o; the first-pass uulgi is corrected without normalization.
The dark end of Desit remains qualified. The dark u in qui and small ring-like marks above the qui/notet area are retained; their exact function is unspecified.
The darker supralinear r in perdita is confirmed; a visible terminal point is restored.
The first s in the final sse of Supposuisse has a darker horizontal stroke. The letter is tentative and no erasure or cancellation is asserted.
Supralinear bi completes main-line credile, and m is added after aliqua. The written components are retained with separate add elements.
The whole source verse is confirmed and its terminal point restored.
The source latis spatiosius in undis is confirmed. A small ring-like supralinear sign over the end of the middle sequence is also retained without assigning a function.
Independent enlargement supports alueus, correcting tentative lacus. The darker second u is retained, with a visible terminal point; no prior overwritten reading is asserted.
The final e of furiose is darker, with the current reading retained.
After per the brown compact group is tentatively tas, with terr written above. The source relation is uncertain; no silent reconstruction of terras is made.
Fontis and the darker e are confirmed. Niuesq is abbreviated in the source, so the previously written-out niuesque is replaced by explicit abbr/expan markup.
The dark/crowded ending of pigra is retained without inventing a prior letter. A visible terminal point is restored.
The dark unq with raised a is an explicit unquam abbreviation; dark si in sitiens is confirmed. The source reads aurire without h, correcting the supplied haurire.
The extra a between perennis and eas has a visible dot beneath it. It is encoded as cancellation by underdot rather than unexplained live text; the surrounding words and terminal sign are confirmed.
The opening is Huc, correcting Huic. Written ue, narrabo and the darker e of amores are confirmed. A pair of oblique marks appears in the right margin.

Spectas has a nasal bar and is expanded spectans. Dark et and barred iac precede brown hon; the barred group is expanded inac. Final amnes has a dark long s. The unusual names and plural ending remain source spellings.
The whole verse and written nile are confirmed. Its visible terminal point and a cross in the right margin are retained.
A long trailing stroke separates the end of this poem from the following enlarged opening of 3.7. The source hyemps spelling is retained.
